title: Bats
subtitle: Seeing with sound
summary: In 1793 Lazzaro Spallanzani blinded bats and found they still flew round a room strung with threads. Nobody could say how until 1938, when a Harvard undergraduate, Donald Griffin, held bats up to a physicist's ultrasonic detector and heard them calling. The course follows the calls from there: why they are so high, how a bat closing on a moth speeds up to 200 a second, and how some moths jam them. Two branches take you outside, to the bats over Green Lake at dusk and to a detector you can build.
